title: Selective learning from the stitched pipeline hypervisor archive

scope.authorization: AUTH-11: user approved the concrete new-archive catalogue proposal with yes.
scope.source_boundary: The 17-file supplied ZIP; prior catalogue used only for explicit learning relationships. Current user requirements are application context.
scope.method: Manual static review of all archive files, including test assertions and supplied results. Long JavaScript listings were read without repetitive blank/comment lines; callable browser/ESM common implementation was reviewed once and wrapper differences separately. No supplied code was executed.
scope.adoption_rule: Do not wholesale adopt code, architecture, taxonomy or claimed guarantees. Every application is not_adopted.
scope.evidence_limit: Static observations and source claims are distinct from assistant interpretations. Predicted failure paths were not reproduced. No independent attestation or benchmark.

source.locator_convention: ZIP-relative paths; 1-based LF-split lines with trailing CR removed and final empty line retained. Excerpts are exact substrings in each declared inclusive range.

taxonomy.status: Assistant working organization approved for this catalogue; not a universal classification or product schema.

categories.lesson: A useful principle supported by the source observation.
categories.anti_lesson: A conclusion or guarantee that should not be inferred from this source.
categories.pattern: A potentially reusable arrangement of responsibilities or behavior.
categories.antipattern: An arrangement unsuitable under the stated application conditions.
categories.structure: A concrete component, record, interface or relationship.
categories.edifice: A larger composition of structures and its operating assumptions.
categories.mechanism: How a behavior is arranged or carried out.
categories.invariant: A condition a future application would need to maintain.
categories.failure_mode: A source-observed gap or a specifically labeled predicted failure.
categories.trade_off: A benefit and cost that depend on purpose or environment.
categories.open_question: A question unresolved by this static review.

application_context.authority: Direct instructions in the current chat; no source-packet or historical TODO grants implementation authority.
constraints: Catalogue lessons and anti-lessons without wholesale adoption.
Native AI-originated documents are the current working assumption; foreign-document reconstruction need not govern the proposed native core.
The user describes direct one-to-one references assembled into words, sentences and paragraphs, with per-system maps including HTML and Python.
Changes produce new streams and retain requested transformations; reduction does not erase their history.
CPU first; later GPU implementation requires a separate scope.
unresolved: Native unit catalogue schema and reference width.
Whether words, sentences and paragraphs are separately interned or only assembled ranges.
Exact codepage contents, return/control semantics and version-binding policy.
Any implementation or runtime validation of the supplied plugin pipeline.

prior_catalogue.boundary: Relationships compare learning records, not an asserted ancestry or verified release history. Earlier records are preserved unchanged.

relationship_types.strengthens: Adds a concrete mechanism relevant to an earlier principle, without proving it complete.
relationship_types.persists: The earlier limitation remains relevant in this source.
relationship_types.qualifies: New source requires a narrower or more differentiated statement.
relationship_types.extends: Adds a related concern or structure.

record_contract.base: Version 2 retains the prior evidence/interpretation/application fields and adds prior_catalogue_links.
record_contract.record_identity: SHH-nnn is a catalogue record identity, not source-defined identity.

entries.title: Separate the original, current value and transformation history

source_evidence.observation: The constructor separates a non-writable original root from current and history properties.
The append method stores a new frozen snapshot alongside the prior entries.

interpretation.text: This is a closer example of retained intermediate values than the earlier shared-context-only model. It remains an in-memory document wrapper.

application.text: Consider separate immutable payloads, current-head references and transformation records for the native model.

limitations: No durable store, content addressing or reduction proof is supplied by this wrapper.
validation_needed: Original and intermediate values remain inspectable after later transformations.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Document payload snapshots now coexist with the mutable context.

entries.title: A frozen history array does not make its owning reference append-only

source_evidence.observation: Current/history fields are writable properties.
The proxy delegates writes to existing wrapper properties.

interpretation.text: A caller with the live document can replace the history or current-root pointer. Frozen entries alone do not establish an enforced append-only API.

application.text: Make history ownership and allowed head changes explicit; expose inspection views rather than writable storage fields.

limitations: No live pointer-replacement attempt was executed.
validation_needed: Replacing history/current pointers through every public access path is rejected where append-only behavior is promised.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The exact immutability boundary still matters.

entries.title: Validate an entire history append before publishing any part

source_evidence.observation: Current root and history are assigned before metadata cloning.
Metadata can still fail strict validation after those assignments.

interpretation.text: Invalid metadata is a predicted path to a changed current root/history without a matching metadata append. The method has no local rollback around that order.

application.text: Prepare and validate the snapshot, metadata and lineage together before publishing one consistent update.

limitations: This exception path was not executed.
validation_needed: Rejected metadata leaves current value, history length and metadata length unchanged.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Publication consistency applies inside the history append too.

entries.title: Protect reserved metadata and define deep immutability

source_evidence.observation: Caller metadata is spread after generated index/event/time fields.
Append metadata is shallow-frozen with caller fields spread last.

interpretation.text: Callers can override reserved descriptive fields, and nested metadata is not recursively frozen by the shallow record freeze. Content and its description have different protection.

application.text: Reserve authoritative identity/order fields and deep-freeze or isolate retained metadata according to a declared contract.

limitations: No metadata override or nested mutation was exercised.
validation_needed: Reserved keys cannot misstate history order; retained nested metadata cannot be mutated through live references.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Metadata protection needs its own depth and authority contract.

entries.title: Preserved history needs a resource and sharing model

source_evidence.observation: Every append clones a full root and copies the growing history array.
Stream output serializes document history together with other state.

interpretation.text: Snapshot retention supports inspection but implies growing copy and serialization work. Repeated array copying can accumulate quadratic reference-copy work with history length; no benchmark was run.

application.text: Separate logical occurrence retention from payload storage and artifact retention; measure sharing and storage costs before selecting a representation.

limitations: No measured memory or timing estimate is claimed.
validation_needed: Long histories stay within explicit byte/time budgets while retaining addressable occurrences.

prior_catalogue_links.note: New history buffers add another retention dimension.

entries.title: Document history is reset when the reader initializes a new pass

source_evidence.observation: Reader initialization replaces both document wrappers and resets revision/analysis state.
The stream reader initializes this state on each execution.

interpretation.text: History is scoped to the current document wrapper, not automatically to all cycles of the running service. Re-reading a source starts new wrappers.

application.text: Specify source ingestion, new-run creation and continuing transformation history as separate operations.

limitations: A reader may intentionally start a fresh document; the issue is the declared lifetime.
validation_needed: A sequence spanning requests retains the intended lineage rather than silently restarting it.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Repeated passes and their input lifetimes need explicit meaning.

entries.title: A no-content-change occurrence need not require another full payload

source_evidence.observation: The stream dummy appends a transformation snapshot even when content is preserved.
The stateful dummy records diagnostics without the stream snapshot operation.

interpretation.text: The two dummy modes distinguish content preservation from the cost of recording it. The source does not deduplicate equal payloads or prove eliminated execution.

application.text: Retain requested no-op occurrences and reasons while allowing equal payload/artifact reuse under the native service contract.

limitations: Equal content does not establish equal provenance or presentation profile.
validation_needed: No-op occurrences remain distinguishable while unnecessary payload copies and rendering can be avoided.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The source explicitly records a stream revision for unchanged content.

entries.title: Use explicit clone contracts for data and trusted runtime objects

source_evidence.observation: The compatibility alias retains runtime-object cloning semantics.
The strict path requires plain objects and checks their own descriptors.

interpretation.text: Splitting strict data cloning from runtime-object cloning is useful. The legacy JsonSafe name no longer communicates the stricter contract.

application.text: Use named, versioned data boundaries; keep executable/runtime objects outside native content records.

limitations: The strict contract intentionally rejects some ordinary JSON object keys such as constructor.
validation_needed: Every call site selects the intended contract; valid-domain exclusions are documented.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Strict data cloning is now separate from general runtime cloning.

entries.title: Array validation must inspect descriptors as well as values

source_evidence.observation: Strict cloning reads array slots directly and returns without inspecting extra own properties.
The plain-object branch explicitly rejects accessors, unlike that array loop.

interpretation.text: An accessor on an array index can be invoked, and extra array properties are not checked by this branch. The README descriptor-rejection claim is broader than these inspected checks.

application.text: Define dense array slots, allowed own keys and descriptor behavior at the native data boundary.

limitations: No getter was invoked during this review; arbitrary Proxy objects need separate consideration too.
validation_needed: Array accessors, symbol/extra keys and non-enumerable slots are accepted or rejected consistently without unintended evaluation.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Stricter object checks do not cover every array shape.

entries.title: Validate address segments before traversing inherited containers

source_evidence.observation: The path converter does not reject prototype-related segments.
The setter traverses indexed containers and assigns before cloning the final root.
Merge traversal also uses inherited property lookup.

interpretation.text: Blocked keys in the final JSON clone do not by themselves protect path traversal. Traversing an inherited prototype container and writing into it is a predicted mutation path before final validation.

application.text: Use a defined address grammar, own-property traversal and reserved-segment checks before any write.

limitations: No prototype mutation or exploit was executed; this is a source-traced concern.
validation_needed: Reserved/inherited path segments cannot modify shared prototypes; failed writes leave all owned and shared state unchanged.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Coordinates also need a safe address-resolution contract.

entries.title: Convenience proxies must preserve host object invariants

source_evidence.observation: The wrapper defines non-configurable own properties.
The proxy ownKeys result uses document-root keys instead of all target keys.

interpretation.text: Omitting non-configurable target keys is a predicted JavaScript Proxy invariant violation for enumeration. Forwarding document fields also collides with wrapper member names.

application.text: Prefer explicit native data accessors or validate every reflection operation if a transparent wrapper is retained.

limitations: Object.keys and related reflection operations were not run.
validation_needed: Enumeration, serialization, member collisions and descriptor queries satisfy the wrapper contract.

prior_catalogue_links.note: A clone/data wrapper must also obey its host runtime invariants.

entries.title: Compatibility methods must state changed behavior

source_evidence.observation: A former replacement flag becomes metadata; commitCurrentRootAsOriginalRoot returns without changing state.

interpretation.text: Retaining an API name while changing its effect can conceal a compatibility break, even when preserving the original root is desirable.

application.text: Use explicit deprecation/outcome records for operations whose old names imply a different effect.

limitations: The archive does not document every historical caller expectation.
validation_needed: Callers receive a clear result for unsupported legacy effects and cannot infer a commit from a method name.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Truthful outcomes include compatibility behavior.

entries.title: Keep current analysis indexes and a state timeline distinct

source_evidence.observation: Generic state stores current per-instance namespace entries plus per-type history and a timeline.
Output snapshot policy can omit type history or timeline.

interpretation.text: This separates current lookup from historical occurrences and reduces output hardwiring to particular analysis plugins.

application.text: Consider derived analysis records keyed to stream, producer occurrence, analysis kind and definition version.

limitations: The source records mutable shared objects rather than an immutable persistent analysis store.
validation_needed: Current and historical reads select the intended stream/producer and preserve older analysis values.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Generic per-instance analysis namespaces extend occurrence-keyed state.

entries.title: Occurrence keys must include their pipeline and run scope

source_evidence.observation: Each plugin manager uses its own local instance counter.
Named pipelines have separate managers but share runtime context.
Generic state is indexed by instance ID without a pipeline field.

interpretation.text: Identical type/counter IDs from separate managers can collide in the shared state bucket. Local uniqueness is narrower than invocation identity.

application.text: Define producer identity with pipeline, instance, invocation and source-stream scope where required.

limitations: The collision sequence was not executed.
validation_needed: Same-type first instances in different named pipelines retain separate state and traces.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Occurrence identity needs a wider scope in a multi-pipeline composition.

entries.title: Visibility labels do not enforce state disclosure policy

source_evidence.observation: State records carry a visibility label.
Snapshot creation clones every instance bucket without filtering visibility.

interpretation.text: A descriptive visibility field is not an access or redaction mechanism. Output consumers need a separate disclosure contract.

application.text: Specify which analysis and metadata fields may enter caller results, debug views and observation summaries.

limitations: No claim is made that the archive is a multi-user service.
validation_needed: Non-public state is excluded from each restricted output surface under explicit policy.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Metadata labels do not isolate authority or disclosure.

entries.title: Analysis tokens still cannot stand in for native content units

source_evidence.observation: The scanner omits whitespace, uses string indices/lengths and lowercases frequency keys.
Frequency storage remains an ordinary object.

interpretation.text: Whitespace/return preservation, UTF-16 coordinate meaning and casefolded derived statistics remain separate concerns from a lossless native reference sequence.

application.text: Keep tokenization optional and derived; define native units, returns, coordinates and map versions independently.

limitations: Original text still exists outside the token list; no Unicode cases were run.
validation_needed: Native round trips preserve all units; analysis coordinates and key domains are explicit.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The tokenizer remains an analysis view.
Index units are still not a native address schema.
Frequency keys still use case folding and ordinary object storage.

entries.title: Text normalization and falsy-root conversion need declared semantics

source_evidence.observation: Non-JSON fallback returns trimmed text.
Context wrapping substitutes an object for a falsy root.
Stream source-text fallback also substitutes for falsy roots.

interpretation.text: Strict JSON scalar support is inconsistent with later truthiness defaults, and source text can lose boundary whitespace.

application.text: Preserve the native source units exactly and distinguish missing values from null, false, zero and empty strings.

limitations: These paths have not been run against a scalar corpus.
validation_needed: Whitespace and every valid scalar receive a documented consistent treatment at all boundaries.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Trimming remains in input normalization.
Truthiness defaults still collapse valid values.

entries.title: Observe execution outside the processing stage sequence

source_evidence.observation: Hook envelopes are cloned and frozen before dispatch.
The hypervisor subscribes to lifecycle hooks instead of loading as a processing node.

interpretation.text: An observation interface can avoid adding document transformations solely to collect telemetry. It still participates in the same process and execution path.

application.text: Consider a versioned observation interface around validated transformation/commit events.

limitations: This is architectural observation, not CPU virtualization or an isolated security monitor.
validation_needed: Observers cannot rewrite authoritative content through their supplied event values.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The source now provides an explicit observation layer.

entries.title: Out-of-band observation can still block and alter the pass

source_evidence.observation: Callbacks execute serially and returned promises are awaited.
Registration accepts execution mode metadata; dispatch has no corresponding mode branch.

interpretation.text: An observer is outside the stage list but still on the execution path. The advertised synchronous/asynchronous label does not select separate scheduling, and a never-settling callback has no dispatch deadline here.

application.text: Define observer scheduling, bounded work, failure and cancellation independently from content transformation.

limitations: No slow or non-settling hook was executed.
validation_needed: Hook deadlines and ordering are enforced; observation cost cannot indefinitely hold a pass.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Observation callbacks add another unbounded evaluation path.

entries.title: Retained dispatch records must track their actual completion

source_evidence.observation: A dispatch record is retained before callbacks run.
Completion updates the local record.
Retention stores a clone rather than the same record.

interpretation.text: The retained clone is not updated by later local counter/completion changes. A snapshot can therefore describe a completed dispatch as unfinished with zero outcomes.

application.text: Use explicit started/completed events or replace a retained record by identity at completion.

limitations: No live hook snapshot was collected.
validation_needed: Returned and retained dispatch outcomes agree after success and each failure policy.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Evidence consistency applies to dispatch journals too.

entries.title: Separate observer failure policy from document transaction outcome

source_evidence.observation: Hook policies distinguish continuation, disablement and pass failure.
Fail-pipeline policy propagates an observer exception after recording it.

interpretation.text: Explicit failure policy is useful, but a failed observer may run after content or output effects. Propagating an exception alone does not roll back those effects.

application.text: Classify mandatory validation, optional telemetry and publication acknowledgements separately, with truthful transaction outcomes.

limitations: The source provides no transaction rollback for arbitrary plugin or sink effects.
validation_needed: Observer failures before and after publication produce documented state and retry behavior.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Failure policy must be aligned with publication.
Telemetry success and authoritative completion are distinct.

entries.title: Reserve event identity fields and define summary disclosure

source_evidence.observation: Caller payload is spread after generated event identity, phase and creation time.
A summary includes up to 50 top-level data keys.
Failure payloads include error summaries, whose helper retains stack text.

interpretation.text: Frozen envelopes can still contain caller-overridden reserved fields; compact summaries and stack text are not a complete disclosure policy.

application.text: Define reserved event fields, redaction rules and bounded summaries as part of the event schema.

limitations: Callbacks are trusted in-process code; this does not claim a demonstrated exfiltration path.
validation_needed: Payload callers cannot override event identity; sensitive names and errors follow explicit disclosure rules.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Event identity and redaction need more than timestamps/freeze.

entries.title: An observational label does not restrict control authority

source_evidence.observation: The hypervisor labels its mode observational.
Its public methods can send runtime signals and request execution.

interpretation.text: This component combines observation and a control facade. It is not an isolated monitor or proof of authority separation.

application.text: Keep observation capabilities, execution requests and approval authority explicit when agentic integration is eventually designed.

limitations: No agentic control is integrated by this review; that remains last.
validation_needed: A read-only consumer cannot acquire control merely through its inspection object.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Names and categories do not confine execution authority.

entries.title: Aggregate metrics without discarding invocation identity

source_evidence.observation: Recent event records retain pipeline/module identity but omit run/cycle and a separate invocation key.
Timing and failure counters aggregate by module type.

interpretation.text: Type-level summaries are useful but cannot answer which repeated or nested invocation caused an observation once detailed events are evicted.

application.text: Retain trace identity separately from aggregate statistics; choose the required run/pipeline/instance/invocation coordinates.

limitations: The source does not promise a durable tracing system.
validation_needed: Repeated nested invocations can be correlated with their start, finish, error and stream result.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Processing occurrences need trace-level identity.
Aggregate telemetry has a specific evidence boundary.

entries.title: Validate dependencies against the actual named pipeline

source_evidence.observation: Named-pipeline construction calls the shared validator.
That validator reads the primary manager warnings.
Order checks still compare first type occurrences and return warnings.

interpretation.text: Structural node checks see the branch nodes, while dependency warning collection still targets the primary manager. Repeated-type and warning-only limitations also remain.

application.text: Resolve dependencies for the actual execution plan and producer occurrence, using explicit errors or warnings by contract.

limitations: No invalid secondary pipeline was executed.
validation_needed: Invalid secondary dependencies and repeated consumer instances are assessed against their own plan.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Warnings are still not execution preconditions.
First-type index comparisons remain.

entries.title: Centralize multi-dimensional pass budgets and report consumption

source_evidence.observation: Each pass initializes a budget state and exposes a snapshot.
Node and branch consumption use named budget-error reasons.
Named-pipeline entry consumes the shared pass branch budget.

interpretation.text: A common budget account is stronger than independent ad hoc caps and supplies useful error context. Its coverage depends on all execution paths participating.

application.text: Consider operation, branch, allocation, output and time budgets with explicit scopes and structured outcomes.

limitations: Source defaults are not recommended production values or measured limits.
validation_needed: Every supported dispatch path consumes the correct account and reports the exhausted dimension.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The source adds explicit per-pass execution accounting.

entries.title: A cooperative elapsed check is not an interrupting deadline

source_evidence.observation: Elapsed time is checked when accounting for another node.
Node execution and hook callbacks run between accounting points.

interpretation.text: A synchronous long node or unresolved promise can exceed the time limit before another check occurs. Node count, input caps and elapsed checks bound different resources.

application.text: Separate cooperative limits from externally enforced worker deadlines where a bounded response is required.

limitations: No blocking workload or timeout was run.
validation_needed: A deliberately stalled operation is terminated or classified within the declared deadline and recovery policy.

prior_catalogue_links.note: A surrounding counter still cannot interrupt one evaluation.

entries.title: Foreach children need the same dispatch and observation contract

source_evidence.observation: The foreach runner calls a child plugin directly instead of the ordinary node dispatcher.
Function mapping also loops internally inside one node.

interpretation.text: Child plugin invocations do not automatically receive ordinary node budget consumption or per-child lifecycle hooks. Item limits help but are a separate bound; passing the same runtime also exposes parent state.

application.text: Route nested work through an explicit child-dispatch interface that carries budgets, identity, state and observation policy.

limitations: No child budget bypass or mutation was exercised; plugins may explicitly consume budgets themselves.
validation_needed: Nested invocations have complete accounting and cannot accidentally operate on parent context/control state.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Coverage must include internal child work.
A child-context wrapper is not execution containment.

entries.title: Acquire the pass guard inside a cleanup-protected region

source_evidence.observation: A pass guard is now set before building executable nodes.
Construction occurs before try/finally; finally normally clears the guard.

interpretation.text: The guard addresses overlapping passes but a synchronous build/validation exception before try can leave it set. The improvement and its uncovered exit path must both be retained.

application.text: Protect guard acquisition, plan validation and cleanup as one lifecycle; return an explicit busy outcome for overlapping requests.

limitations: No overlapping or build-failure call was run.
validation_needed: Every setup failure releases the guard; concurrent requests get a truthful outcome.

prior_catalogue_links.note: A single-flight guard now exists, but its setup region has a gap.

entries.title: Pause and reset need a generation and continuation contract

source_evidence.observation: Traversal returns its context at pause/stop.
The patched completion path preserves PAUSED.
Reset replaces the context without a generation token.

interpretation.text: Pause preservation is improved over the base run method, but runOnce builds from the start rather than a saved continuation. Reset during an awaited node still needs a stale-completion policy.

application.text: Specify restart versus resume, frozen input/configuration, cancellation generation and late-result rejection.

limitations: Resume/reset timing cases were not reproduced; the supplied pause test only checks stopping before output.
validation_needed: Pause/resume avoids accidental repeated effects; reset prevents old completions from replacing the new context.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Patched pause preservation is present; continuation/generation requirements remain.

entries.title: Nested errors must propagate to the final pass outcome

source_evidence.observation: A node failure records an error and returns context rather than throwing.
The recursion entry checks pause/stop but not ERROR.
The outer pass emits finished after traversal returns, including error-state returns.

interpretation.text: A nested branch can return an error-state context to its caller, which may still continue through later nodes. Finished describes control return, not necessarily successful transformation; context.status can also lag the runtime state.

application.text: Use one explicit result contract for success, partial effects, failed child work and publication eligibility.

limitations: Nested error continuation and status divergence are source-traced predictions, not runtime results.
validation_needed: Inner errors suppress unauthorized downstream publication and produce consistent event/state outcomes.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Multiple state fields and completion labels remain ambiguous.

entries.title: Prototype patching makes assembly order part of behavior

source_evidence.observation: Loading the control-flow file patches a shared runtime prototype once.
The original executor is retained, then patch installation runs at load.
The page selects a specific script load order.

interpretation.text: The stitched runtime is defined by source composition and load order, not solely pipeline-core.js. A review or test of only the base runtime can miss effective behavior.

application.text: Prefer explicit runtime extension/composition contracts and capture the implementation/configuration identity used by a plan.

limitations: No alternative script order or reload was executed.
validation_needed: All supported entry points select the same intended runtime semantics without hidden global patch dependence.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The larger composition now includes runtime replacement behavior.

entries.title: Signal-driven skipping is distinct from proven transformation reduction

source_evidence.observation: A filter converts an external signal to a next-module decision.
The executor records and skips the next non-system node.

interpretation.text: A recorded conditional skip is not a proof that two requested transformations cancel or that their dependencies permit omission. It also depends on the current stage adjacency.

application.text: Preserve the distinction between future user-selectable bypass and the current requirement to reduce logically redundant work with reasons.

limitations: The user has deferred selective bypass; source capability does not change that decision.
validation_needed: Any optimization explains its semantic preconditions and retains requested transformation occurrences.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Inspectable order can also contain signal-dependent skips.
Do not import unrelated behavior because it exists in the archive.

entries.title: Regex heuristics and input caps are useful but incomplete bounds

source_evidence.observation: Regex creation rejects selected nested-group/alternation/wildcard patterns and caps source length.
The shared search helper caps input length before constructing a scanner.
The advanced matchesRegex path calls test without that search-helper input cap.

interpretation.text: There are now useful defensive checks, but heuristic rejection is not an exhaustive complexity proof and not every regex caller uses the same caps.

application.text: Centralize regex policy if retained; bound every caller and select an execution model with the required worst-case behavior.

limitations: No pathological pattern was run; heuristic false positives/negatives are unmeasured.
validation_needed: Every regex call path follows documented limits and cancellation behavior with representative adversarial cases.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Heuristics and input caps were added but do not guarantee a deadline.

entries.title: Scanners need coordinate-correct progress and completion labels

source_evidence.observation: Zero-width progress still advances one string unit.
A capped scan returns the same result shape without a completion/truncation field.

interpretation.text: The match prefix can be mistaken for a complete result, and one-unit advancement still requires Unicode-mode analysis. A returned match count alone is not a completeness claim.

application.text: Expose complete/capped/failed state and define coordinates/progress independently of native stream addressing.

limitations: Unicode zero-width scans and cap-boundary cases were not executed.
validation_needed: Empty matches make correct forward progress and capped results cannot be presented as exhaustive.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The zero-width and truncation questions remain.

entries.title: Optional predicate values must survive strict-boundary migration

source_evidence.observation: Predicate evaluation permits an absent expected value.
The returned record unconditionally strict-clones expectedValue and non-sentinel actualValue.
The JSON-branch default can leave that value undefined.

interpretation.text: Unary/default predicates can compute a result and then fail while constructing their diagnostic record, because undefined is rejected by the strict clone. An absent external signal can similarly reach that boundary.

application.text: Represent missing values explicitly and validate configuration by operator; audit callers when a clone contract becomes stricter.

limitations: These advanced predicate defaults were not executed; their supplied test coverage is assessed separately.
validation_needed: Unary operators and absent signals produce intentional typed outcomes rather than a recording-time exception.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Missing and valid values need explicit semantics at analysis boundaries.
Changing clone strictness requires call-site migration.

entries.title: Packaged operations and arbitrary callbacks have different authority

source_evidence.observation: Built-in item processing uses a finite named operation set.
A custom mapper instead receives full context, runtime and plugin references.
Child plugin selection can resolve a global path.

interpretation.text: Closed built-ins are a useful service model. A callback or global-name lookup is trusted executable configuration, not ordinary safe request data.

application.text: Keep the eventual agent-facing request API closed over packaged validated operations; avoid request-selected code or global callable resolution.

limitations: No request-facing agent integration is supplied or enabled by this review.
validation_needed: Untrusted callers cannot submit callbacks or expand capability through arbitrary global paths.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Code categories and data wrappers do not isolate execution.

entries.title: Object conversions need explicit key and type-loss rules

source_evidence.observation: Map creation coerces supported input keys to strings.
Map-to-object output uses ordinary object assignment.
Emitters distinguish runtime object values from their JSON representations.

interpretation.text: Runtime objects and their interchange representation are different artifacts. String coercion can merge keys, and ordinary object assignment needs a reserved-key policy.

application.text: Define reversible codecs or report intentional losses for any native/interchange conversion.

limitations: No collision or prototype-key case was executed; string-key-only contracts may intentionally constrain the domain.
validation_needed: Key collisions, ordering and type changes are detected or explicitly accepted.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Declared data support does not define conversion fidelity.

entries.title: Reconstruct trusted behavior from registered definitions and state

source_evidence.symbol: State is cloneable data. Behavior is registered and reconstructed.
source_evidence.excerpt: State is cloneable data. Behavior is registered and reconstructed.
source_evidence.observation: The module states a separation between state and registered behavior.
A registered callable clones constructor/internal data and asks the trusted factory for a function.
Callable cloning allocates a shell before recursively copying its state.

interpretation.text: This is a useful conceptual separation for reproducible operation definitions. Factory execution still has arbitrary trusted-code effects and is not a sandbox.

application.text: Represent transformation kind/version and immutable arguments separately from packaged evaluator behavior.

limitations: No callable machinery is adopted; native character/unit lookup is a different responsibility.
validation_needed: Only approved definitions resolve; reconstructed behavior has defined state and capability boundaries.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Definition, state and occurrence can be separated explicitly.
Registration defines a trust boundary but does not contain factory behavior.

entries.title: Duplicate rejection and schema labels do not bind behavior versions

source_evidence.observation: Callable duplicate registration is rejected by default but configurable.
Descriptor recognition checks kind/type ID without checking schemaVersion.
Reconstruction uses the current registry binding and omits descriptor metadata.
The separate plugin registry still replaces entries by type.

interpretation.text: There are multiple registration contracts. A callable type name or emitted schemaVersion does not ensure the same historical definition will be reconstructed later.

application.text: Bind native maps and transformation definitions to explicit immutable identities and validated schema/version policies.

limitations: No cross-version descriptor was rehydrated; duplicate rejection is a real improvement in its own registry.
validation_needed: Unknown schema versions and changed definitions are rejected or migrated explicitly; old streams retain meaning.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Callable duplicate rejection is stronger, while plugin replacement and version binding remain separate.

entries.title: A declared clone option must actually control its copy paths

source_evidence.observation: The engine stores an accessor-policy option.
Descriptor copying preserves accessors without consulting that option.
Ordinary object cloning uses the descriptor helper.

interpretation.text: The inspected copy path does not enforce allowAccessors:false. Rejecting raw function values does not also reject getter/setter functions retained inside descriptors.

application.text: Use policies whose enforcement is traceable at every relevant branch; keep runtime cloning distinct from strict native data validation.

limitations: No accessor object was executed; defaults intentionally permit accessors.
validation_needed: Setting each public policy option changes the promised behavior or is rejected as unsupported.

prior_catalogue_links.note: A hardening name or policy field is not proof of enforcement.

entries.title: Graph cloning must preserve aliasing as well as cycles

source_evidence.observation: ArrayBuffer and shared-buffer clones do not register the new buffer in seen here.
Views clone their buffers through that branch.
The included clone self-test checks one ordinary-object cycle.

interpretation.text: Two views sharing a source buffer can be reconstructed over separate buffer copies; repeated special-object references also need a consistent alias policy. A cycle test does not establish full graph fidelity.

application.text: Define which alias relationships are meaningful for any future binary/native storage implementation and test them explicitly.

limitations: No shared-buffer clone was executed. This applies to the callable clone engine; the core manual clone has a different buffer-map implementation.
validation_needed: Shared views, repeated references, offsets and independent mutations preserve the declared graph semantics.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Clone correctness includes relationships among values, not just individual values.

entries.title: Cloning a callable reference must not silently change its representation

source_evidence.observation: CallableRef.rehydrate expects a descriptor.
Generic clone converts recognized descriptors into runtime callables.
Cloning a CallableRef sends its descriptor through that same conversion path.

interpretation.text: A cloned reference can receive a runtime callable where its rehydrate method expects descriptor data. Descriptor materialization and data cloning are conflated.

application.text: Make inert references, executable reconstruction and serialized descriptors separate explicit operations.

limitations: This sequence was not executed; the supplied callable self-test does not cover CallableRef.
validation_needed: A cloned reference remains a valid inert reference and rehydrates only at the intended boundary.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Copying data should not implicitly change representation or activate behavior.

entries.title: Twin entry points require parity checks and honest runner evidence

source_evidence.observation: The browser build publishes a global namespace/CommonJS export.
The original module exposes ESM exports.
The main runner selects the browser shim rather than the ESM module.
A separate ESM runner exists.

interpretation.text: Text comparison shows the shared implementation matches, with packaging/example/export differences. One runner loading the shim is not proof that both entry points execute successfully in their intended hosts.

application.text: Maintain one implementation source or checked build parity, and validate supported entry points separately when authorized.

limitations: No Node, ESM or browser entry point was executed; no package.json is present in the supplied inventory.
validation_needed: Generated and source variants stay aligned, and each declared host entry point has its own recorded result.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Artifact packaging and executed validation have separate proof boundaries.

entries.title: Test names must be read against their actual assertions

source_evidence.observation: The node-budget test checks both error state/reason and absence of output.
The lifecycle-order test asserts first/last events and membership rather than the entire sequence.
The runner lists 16 tests with no direct advanced plugin test functions.

interpretation.text: Narrow negative assertions are useful. Loading a module or giving a test a broad name does not establish all behaviors, event permutations, elapsed deadlines, concurrency or advanced-plugin correctness.

application.text: Keep requirements-to-assertion coverage explicit in future rigid, fuzzy and torture suites.

limitations: This review reads tests without running them; it does not alter the existing Docstream harness.
validation_needed: Tests cover both success and forbidden side effects at each promised boundary; coverage gaps remain visible.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Source assertions let the supplied evidence be assessed more precisely.

entries.title: Retain supplied results as dated claims with a provenance boundary

source_evidence.observation: The report declares overall success.
Its internal completion timestamp predates this October intake.
The README also presents an expected success result.

interpretation.text: The report contains 16 reported passes, but does not bind them to an archive digest or record a host/runtime identity. Its timestamp is a source claim, not an authenticated execution time.

application.text: Preserve supplied reports separately from fresh local runs and independent attestation, with source and implementation identities.

limitations: No claim is made that the supplied report is false or that it was produced from this exact archive.
validation_needed: A future run records tested bytes, environment, command, outcome and retained failures.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Time and logs alone are not independent attestation.
A packaged passed report is not current validation.

entries.title: Separate human inspection surfaces from document rendering

source_evidence.observation: The UI separates running/input/configuration/debug/oversight into tabs.
Output is rendered as text rather than inserted as active HTML.
The file-reader path has a two-million-byte cap.
Responsive rules change inspection layout without defining document pagination.

interpretation.text: Providers/sinks and distinct inspection surfaces remain useful. A file-only size check and JSON display do not establish all input limits, accessibility or document-render fidelity.

application.text: Keep core service outputs distinct from optional human inspection; define limits on every request/input path.

limitations: No browser layout, keyboard interaction or accessibility behavior was executed.
validation_needed: All input modes enforce their contracts and inspection layout is visually/interaction tested in a later authorized scope.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Adapter boundaries remain explicit.
Tabs separate views, although regex/tests still write into the shared output pane.
Inspector CSS is not a document rendering contract.

entries.title: Distinguish configured factories, loaded instances and live signals

source_evidence.observation: Applying branch configuration replaces installed factory definitions.
The UI updates signals and branch factories from mutable controls.
Loading constructs an instance whose configuration is then retained in that instance.
Regex settings are read live from controls.

interpretation.text: Some configuration is captured in loaded instances, while other values are read during execution. An inspector showing current controls may not describe the exact plan being executed.

application.text: Capture validated configuration and signal policy in a plan identity; expose pending versus active configuration.

limitations: No live reconfiguration race was executed.
validation_needed: A run is reproducible from its recorded configuration and mid-run changes have an explicit next-run or live-control policy.

prior_catalogue_links.note: A replaced factory does not automatically update existing occurrences.
Reproducibility needs actual configuration identity.

entries.title: A processor registry and JSON history are not the native reference core

source_evidence.observation: Document authority is represented through JSON-compatible roots and copies.
Text analysis produces string-valued tokens and numeric offsets.
Advanced foreach transforms operate on JSON arrays and named item operations.

interpretation.text: Across the 17-file source there is no implementation of the proposed native character/control-unit maps and direct reusable word/sentence/paragraph assemblies. More orchestration does not supply that data model.

application.text: Design the native unit catalogue, definition binding, assembly addressing and representation separately, using selected principles only.

limitations: This absence statement is limited to the supplied archive; no reference width, mandatory interning or codepage meaning is prescribed.
validation_needed: A later design explicitly defines native units and assembly semantics before implementation or migration.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The native reference data plane remains a distinct design task.

entries.title: Health is a policy over recent evidence, not an attestation

source_evidence.observation: Health uses runtime error state and the last 25 retained alerts.
Namespace availability is tested by object presence.
Timing accepts finite durations and aggregates them; runtime durations are measured using Date.now.

interpretation.text: Nominal health means these local checks found no qualifying alert. It does not prove correct processing, executable namespace compatibility, recovery or independent oversight. Count-based recency is not elapsed-time recency.

application.text: Define health states in terms of observable conditions, coverage, staleness and recovery; retain monotonic duration semantics where needed.

limitations: No clock jump or alert-aging scenario was run.
validation_needed: Missing/stale coverage and recovered errors are represented truthfully without confusing presence with capability.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Local telemetry establishes only its stated observations.

entries.title: Output assignment, sink success and pass completion are separate events

source_evidence.observation: Output is assigned and a stream record appended before sink.write, then a diagnostic follows.
The stateful path follows the same sequence.

interpretation.text: A sink failure can leave output/emission state indicating prepared data while delivery failed. The snapshot also precedes its own output-written diagnostic and later stages.

application.text: Define prepared, published, committed and inspected outcomes separately; publish a receipt consistent with the final state.

limitations: No failing sink was executed; external side effects may require their own idempotency contract.
validation_needed: Sink failure and late-stage failure cannot be mistaken for committed/published success, and retries are explicit.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Publication and evidence still need a consistent transaction boundary.

entries.title: Edifice: stitched oversight around a mutable execution system

source_evidence.symbol: This build stitches together the uploaded parts:
source_evidence.excerpt: This build stitches together the uploaded parts:
source_evidence.observation: The README describes assembling separate source packages.
The page composes core, adapters, processing, control, advanced, callable, oversight, tests and UI scripts.
Oversight cloning has fallback paths with different value semantics.
The oversight snapshot reports callable-registry presence and self-test availability; its clone helper instead selects core/platform/JSON implementations.

interpretation.text: The useful larger arrangement is document snapshots plus a mutable orchestration/context layer, hooks, an oversight facade and human inspection. Global composition, fallback contracts and trust assumptions remain part of that arrangement. Callable cloning remains a sibling facility; its presence in the bundle does not mean the core or oversight copy paths use it.

application.text: Adapt individual responsibilities through explicit interfaces; retain the CPU service as reference and integrate agentic control only at the final stage.

limitations: This review proves no successful stitched boot, durable service, GPU backend or security containment.
validation_needed: Any later proposal names adopted principles, rejected assumptions, component identities and conformance checks.

prior_catalogue_links.note: The source is a larger browser demonstrator with supervision and history.
Selective learning remains the approved method.

entries.title: Equality helpers need a declared semantic domain

source_evidence.observation: Deep equality sorts object keys and compares JSON serialization.
Strict predicates use a different equality operation.

interpretation.text: The source offers useful deterministic key ordering for a JSON comparison, but that is not automatically the semantic equivalence needed for native units, numeric edge cases, style inheritance or artifact reuse.

application.text: Define content equality, definition identity, occurrence identity and rendering-profile equality independently before optimizer or cache rules use them.

limitations: No numeric or normalization edge cases were tested; this review does not choose the native equality policy.
validation_needed: Every reduction/cache comparison declares its domain and preserves all distinctions significant to that domain.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Identity and content equality answer different questions.
A no-op requires a defined content equivalence relation.

entries.title: Bound record counts, payload bytes and key cardinality separately

source_evidence.observation: Recent event arrays have explicit count caps.
Aggregate metric dictionaries have no per-key cardinality cap in these declarations/use paths.
Generic state histories append without a retention cap.
Context diagnostics/errors/stream append independently of debug retention.

interpretation.text: Bounded oversight arrays do not bound total process state. Payload size, number of distinct names, full snapshot history and repeated serialization can dominate count-limited logs.

application.text: Specify retention by purpose and account for bytes, keys and nested values as well as record counts; preserve durable lineage outside ephemeral telemetry limits.

limitations: No memory growth, leak or throughput measurement was performed.
validation_needed: Long and high-cardinality workloads stay within explicit budgets without erasing authoritative history.

prior_catalogue_links.note: Some oversight records are now bounded; whole-system retention is not.
